corrections.was: Now a mesh is bound to the bones. The Rest pose, also called the bind pose, is the skeleton's default pose, the one the mesh was fitted to. Here every angle is zero and the arm is straight. Bend the elbow with each point tied to only one bone, and the mesh tears at the joint. For example, a character modelled in Blender standing straight with arms out is bound in that pose, and you can return the skeleton to it at any time.
corrections.now: Now a mesh is bound to the bones. The Rest pose, also called the bind pose, is the skeleton's default pose, the one the mesh was fitted to. Here every angle is zero and the arm is straight. Bend the elbow with each point tied to only one bone, and the mesh splits at the joint. For example, a character modelled in Blender standing straight with arms out is bound in that pose, and you can return the skeleton to it at any time.
corrections.why: Voice rule: say.py reads 'tears' as the crying noun (t-ee-rz), so 'tears' became 'splits'; the meaning (a rigid binding opens a gap at the elbow) is unchanged.

corrections.was: Second, which interpolation sits between the keys? Linear, step and cubic fill the same gaps differently, and only step holds a value and then jumps.
corrections.now: Second, what sits between the keys? Linear, step and cubic fill the same gaps differently, and only step holds a value and then jumps.
corrections.why: Calling step an interpolation repeats the slide's mix-up. Chapter 10 'Between keys' lists interpolation as nearest, linear or cubic, and discrete as a separate update mode, so the question no longer files step under interpolation.

corrections.was: Fifth, does the loop close? The last key should equal the first, so there is no loop seam each time the clip wraps.
corrections.now: Fifth, is the loop closed? The last key should equal the first, so there is no loop seam each time the clip wraps.
corrections.why: Voice rule: say.py reads 'close' here as the adjective (klohs), so the question was reworded to 'is the loop closed', which it reads correctly.
